thread.title: Micron And Texas Instruments Warned Us About Tech - Micron Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MU)

author: Elazar Advisors, LLC
title: Micron And Texas Instruments Warned Us About Tech - Micron Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MU)
text:
If you listened to Micron (NASDAQ: MU ) or Texas Instruments (NASDAQ: TXN ) earnings calls you should have been shocked. If you were, kudos. Micron was saying there's a multi-quarter inventory correction coming. TI was saying between the lines that the cycle's peaked. That can mean a down year ahead.
Let's review.
In tech we care very much about the supply chain because when one piece slows it can slow all the hand-offs in that food chain. As things slow based on one reason or the other it causes the other players in the supply chain to get more conservative.
Then you have it snowball, and that's called a cycle.
Semiconductors are known to be in cycles. We've had a couple of years up and we're probably headed into a year or so down.
We've been bearish about semiconductors to subscribers for months and I continue to be bearish on the group. I'm not picking bottoms just yet.
Stocks Help You On Stocks But Also Help You On The Big Picture When you hear something great or something wrong in the space you have to take note. When it's something that sounds broad based like "across the board" or "multiple customers" you have to think that may affect other players in the space.
When we heard sweeping-type remarks from TI and Micron we took note for the entire space. TI and Micron make chips that are in just about everything. So you have to take note. Here's what we found and said and it very much matters here and now.
What Did Texas Instruments Say On Their Earnings?
Here's what TI said last quarter October 23:
".. .demand for our products slowed across most markets during the quarter."
That shocked us.
TI sells into a wide range of geographies and end markets. When you hear a company like this say they're seeing weakness across the board you have to pay attention.
They also hinted that their cycles of two years up and one year down may have completed the up part of the cycle.
When asked if we're going into a downturn they answered:
"Yes, I’d start that as we look at those, and we all look at industry data. As we went through those other downturns, the ups weren’t very strong and therefore the downs weren’t very strong, right? And I think we’ve just described those as we’ve moved through them. It’s just operating in a world that really have low economic growth, right? So the last couple of years, certainly, we’ve had much stronger upturn in the economy overall. The economic growth has been stronger over the last couple of years. So that’s certainly different."
What's different? The last 10 years had mini ups and downs because the economy wasn't so robust to pull the rubber band too far.
What's different this time is the "last couple of years, certainly, we've had much stronger upturn" which means the snap back lower can be more meaningful too.
That's something serious.
TI typically has two years up, one year down.
While everybody's looking to pick bottoms I think investors have been way too spoiled by slow years in the economy and finally a rush of good in the last two years. But a tech heavyweight is telling you the that the up we just had tells you how big the down can be.
I think it's worth being careful.
Sure we can have bounces along the way. But, for now at least, the general fundamental direction is for slowing.
Here's what we said after that earnings call to subscribers ( pay wall ) on Oct 23 which is just as relevant today. We took that TI call and we made it important to the rest of tech, which it was.
"As you know we've been cautious on semiconductor stocks for a while.
You also saw our preview that we were below the street for TXN earnings and cautious ahead of this earnings report tonight.
The stock is down and I expect it can drop further.
I have to say this earnings report was worse than I expected. The company said they saw a slowdown across the board in all their end markets. That is a very serious statement.
I pointed out in the preview that their two-year revenue growth was slowing. In fact their guide slowed to 0% revenue growth.
If investors had any cycle fears they are coming true with a bellwether now at flat revenue growth.
Look at this "fast" slowdown.
Q2 Q3 Q4 Q1 Q2 Q3 Q4 2017 2017 2017 2018 2018 2018 2018 A E Revenues 3693 4116 3750 3789 4017 4261 3750 Growth 12.8% 12.0% 9.8% 8.6% 8.8% 3.5% 0.0% 2yr 14.1% 19.2% 16.9% 24.6% 21.6% 15.5% 9.8% Two-year goes from 24.6 to 21.6 to 15.5 (which we pointed out in the preview) to now the guide of 9.8% and a 0% 1 year. That 0% Q4 guide quickly slowed from 10-12% just a few quarters ago.
TXN revenues move with GDP historically so this is a tech and an economic datapoint.
TXN's chart with this after market move will now be at multi year lows.
Even though stocks are down, the news just got worse specifically in semiconductor land.
TXN didn't know the reason for the slowdown which also is troubling. If you can put your finger on it we know what to watch. But if they don't know and the slowdown is across the board, that is something to pay attention to.
This is a time not to be complacent on stocks hoping they go higher. I think we will continue to let the market dictate the trend but slowing fundamentals have to be recognized.
I had said that stocks don't get hit on media reports but do get hit on earnings. That's what's happening.
Cycle peak worries are getting confirmed.
Not great."
You can see we wanted to be clear, there was risk ahead. Our concerns on semis were getting proven out with a bellwether saying everything is slowing. They also hinted that the drop could be bigger than past drops.
We point out TI because when institutional investors think TI they think about broad customer bases and they think about their inventory channel and cycles. We're likely headed to a down cycle or we're at the early innings and other companies can likely be affected.
Same Thing With Micron Here's what Micron said on their last earnings call before tech earnings season really got under way back in September.
"I don’t know exactly how long the CPU shortage will last. I think on the inventory correction side, it will be a couple of quarters before inventory gets reduced."
In tech it's so important to be cognizant of the "tech food chain" or the tech supply chain. When one piece in that food chain slows down the rest of the chain, like dominoes, can easily get affected. Then companies in that supply chain have to slow purchases and it cycles through to other companies. That's one reason why it's called a cycle.
Micron, with their inventory channel comments, told us to watch out going forward. There's been a ton of bulls on Micron but comments like several quarters of channel issues is a cycle peak call out.
When we heard Micron talk about a channel build up we immediately thought about the tech space. Just like TI, Micron's chips are in pretty much everything. If they are seeing a backed-up channel because demand slowed, well, demand probably slowed.
This was our reaction for tech in general ( pay wall ) after that Micron earnings call back on September 20th and I think this is early innings so still very relevant today,
"Overall I think end demand for tech is strong but there are some serious headwinds that need to be considered at least through this next earnings season. It could mean that the top end of demand growth comes off.
*Micron said tariffs will hurt them for the next few quarters. Other companies will say that. Even our buys. A few quarters? That's a long time to stare down negative news headwinds. We can't just brush that off. When I see it show up in their earnings on our other buys I will also move to neutral. In the meantime I will keep sizing low and only buy when I see it moving in an uptrend.
Trump tweeting about tariffs isn't the risk catalyst for the stocks. I've said when tariffs hit earnings, that's the risk catalyst. Earnings are what drives stocks. Micron said tariffs now cause risk for them for several quarters. I take that datapoint to mean other tech companies are going to say the same thing. That's reason to be cautious.
I don't think we want to lug around tech risk for several quarters because of tariffs hitting earnings. We need to pick our points which is what I want to do.
China just backed off further negotiations and while the market seems like it goes up every day which needs to be respected a hit to earnings is a real stock market risk. I don't want to be lazy about what's likely coming.
I don't think Trump loses votes from a trade war but rather rallies his contingent. That would mean that into mid-term elections in November the cries that China is unfair could only get louder. That can rally his base.
*PC delays because of Intel shortage will affect many in that food chain.
*It's very good that Samsung is pulling back on supply but it also means that it's a reaction because of the lost level of profitability. In NAND that's demand related. Does that go away? I don't think Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) drives huge incremental demand, they are not going for unit growth but rather price. For DRAM there is a touch weaker demand if pricing is coming down, as well.
Remember investors were surprised to hear from Arista at a recent conference that they are not seeing 50% growth from 50% CAPEX budget growth numbers at cloud companies. So it's not one-for-one down to the tech companies.
*I don't love the GPU gaming food chain either because of too much supply.
There's enough reasons to continue to be cautious on semis and tech that tend to trade together.."
Ahead of earnings season Micron gave us enough to take seriously about the risk for tech. We advised subscribers be 100% hedged through October and most of November (except for like one day - the post-midterm rally day).
I don't see any change. If anything we're only at the very start of worsening fundamentals.
How To Pick A Bottom Numbers for many companies like Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN ), Apple, Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA ), AMD (NASDAQ: AMD ), Micron and Texas Instruments all started slowing in Q3.
I think it makes sense to wait until Q2 2019 when you're about to "lap" those slowing growth rates. That can make next year's growth rates stop slowing and start reaccelerating. But that's not until Q3 or Q4 of 2019.
Valuations don't necessarily bottom stocks. Hope for a turnaround or any hints to a turnaround bottom stocks.
Tech stocks run on momentum. That's fundamental momentum. Are growth rates moving up or slowing? That's what most of the money that pushes around tech stocks cares about.
That realistic turn can come in the form of easier growth comparisons but not until the second half of 2019.
Keep in mind that TI typically has two years up, one year down for their semi cycles. So that one-year clock just started ticking. That also coincides with a second half 2019 opportunity.
As I mentioned above, that's a long time to lug around ideas.
Conclusion It's easy to get bearish now when stocks are showing it but I think it's more important to not get lazy when a company's story changes. The best investors and traders I've seen are super sensitive to changing dynamics.
When I say a company's story changes I mean their earnings story. I've said it on many reports that media or Trump tweets are not the ultimate driver to stock prices. Earnings are. And that earnings story has just changed. Micron and TI were two important precursors to pay attention to.
